This section evaluates whether observation-aware stabilization (OAS) improves task performance, training dynamics, and search-budget control. We examine final QA performance across datasets, retrieval budgets, and model sizes; evaluate bounded transfer to FEVER fact verification; analyze how nVDD, ATE, AUS, and OAGC evolve together with EM; and study retrieval behavior and search-budget use during training.

We use a Search-R1-style search-tool RL framework on three benchmark datasets: NQ, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA. During each rollout, the model generates search actions, the retriever inserts observation tokens into the context, and the model continues reasoning before producing a final answer. Main-text experiments use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (Yang et al., 2024), with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct used as an additional scale check. We report final EM across datasets and Top-k budgets with k ∈ {2, 3, 5}. We analyze nVDD, ATE, and OAGC in the Qwen2.5-3B Top-3 ablations, and time-align EM, nVDD, ATE, AUS, and OAGC for the controlled Qwen2.5-1.5B NQ Top-3 PPO and OAS trajectories. The OAS defaults are αmin = 0.2000, β = 0.2812, λobs = 1.0000, and λsm = 0.0277: all were frozen before formal evaluation. All methods within a setting use the same split, retrieval budget, generation limits, and exact-match scorer; full dataset, baseline, coefficient-selection, and sensitivity details are in Appendix D.

We first compare OAS with baselines on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, testing task performance across datasets and retrieval budgets. Table 2 reports mean (sample SD) over two runs for the main 3B comparison. OAS has a higher reported two-run mean than Search-R1 PPO in all nine settings and the highest mean among all compared methods in eight of nine settings. Under the Top-3 setting, its means are 37.6/56.8/23.9 EM on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA, compared with 31.8/49.6/18.7 for Search-R1 PPO. OVR-only is already competitive, consistent with observation-side value regularization and residual decay contributing to the gain; full OAS has higher means than OVR-only in all nine settings, consistent with an additional contribution from boundary smoothing. The pattern is not tied to a single Top-k: NQ and TriviaQA have their highest OAS means at Top-3, while HotpotQA has its highest OAS mean at Top-5. Multi-hop questions can benefit from additional evidence, whereas shorter factoid questions may suffer from irrelevant observations and a heavier context-modeling burden.

To examine OAS beyond open-domain QA, we evaluate it on FEVER fact verification (Thorne et al.,2018) using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. FEVER assigns each claim one of three labels—SUPPORTS, REFUTES, or NOT ENOUGH INFO—using Wikipedia evidence. Each claim receives one fixed Top-3 retrieval, and PPO and OAS share the claims, observations, data order, training budget, reward, and evaluation protocol. We evaluate search-on three-way label accuracy at steps 25, 50, and 75 and compute nVDD over the same validation sequence.
